review: External privileged SECURITY DEFINER delegation counterexample

findings.title: Protection activation misses callable privileged wrappers outside the truss schema
findings.observation: A pre-existing public.preexisting_raw_resource() SQL SECURITY DEFINER owned by the original runtime owner remains callable by the ordinary actor after successful activation and commit. The ordinary actor has no direct truss.object SELECT but receives all six raw property bags, including denied r2 salary 9007199254740993, its opaque token and private Assignment values.
findings.mechanism: Routine grant census/revocation and verification are restricted to namespace truss. The external function delegates the excluded runtime owner authority and therefore falls outside that inventory even though it reads the protected store.
findings.requiredDisposition: Do not qualify installation-wide protection until activation/current verification refuses or closes unqualified reachable privileged delegation outside the schema, including applicable definer/view/dependency routes. Preserve this exact pre-activation wrapper as a regression; later hostile DDL is not necessary for the counterexample.

independentWork.scope: Read-only source and retained native observation review; original parent run reused.

nativeWitness.activation: Original activation returned Ok; inherited create_query_graph asserts success and commits before ordinary calls.
nativeWitness.guardedPath: The invoked original positive method separately passes masked salary, exact neighboring integer exclusion, prohibited ORDER and public byte-limit assertions.
nativeWitness.bypass: Same test then opens an ordinary consumer, observes direct raw SELECT false, and successfully calls the pre-existing outside-schema function.
nativeWitness.cleanup: Retained runtime stopped, lease released and test-directory-absent flags are true.

governingRequirement.contract: CONTRACT-063 NativeInventory requires all reachable privileges/definer transitions and excludes ordinary reachability of installer/integrity roles through callable wrappers.
governingRequirement.US-056-AC5: The successful external wrapper is an indirect bypass path to protected raw data.
governingRequirement.US-056-AC8: The same wrapper returns hidden Assignment properties used for authorization.
governingRequirement.acceptanceEffect: Negative discovery evidence only; no case promotion or requirement change.

scopeAndCustodyLimits: The source is an uncommitted Truss working snapshot, not a fixed release/main qualification. All 1142 retained pre-run source pins still match; this review does not retroactively create a post-run source-attestation record.
The separately copied binding fixture was omitted from the original snapshot-pins map. Its current retained hash is recorded explicitly as observed now, not as a before-run pin.

The harness prepends the previously extracted ABI2 wheel and source/test paths, but does not record actual imported module/native executable path hashes. No complete wheel/native-binary/process attestation is claimed for this probe.

The function is deliberately installed by the excluded admin immediately before activation. This demonstrates an existing delegation that activation failed to exclude, not an ordinary ability to create privileged functions or a post-activation hostile-DDL schedule.
The one executed method does not run the separate FALSE/empty or all-denied workflow methods. Those source methods being present is not execution evidence.
No separate actual postmaster-PID absence observation is present in this probe. Runtime/lease/directory cleanup checks are retained; prior replay PID evidence is not inherited.
No claim is made about every external function language/dependency, view, cached plan, shared catalog or subsequent repair. Partner implementation/review remains separate.
